question: Why are neutrons important for the stability of heavy nuclei? Explain with reference to electrostatic repulsion and nuclear force.

options.A: Neutrons are important because they increase electrostatic repulsion between protons.
options.B: Neutrons are electrically neutral, so they add no Coulomb repulsion but contribute to attractive nuclear force between nucleons. Thus, in heavy nuclei they help counter proton-proton repulsion and improve stability.
options.C: Neutrons are important because they convert all protons into electrons inside the nucleus.
options.D: Neutrons are unnecessary because nuclear force acts only between protons.
